clue.text: Venerable soothsayer not right with first couple of statements

indicators.note: the word for soothsayer must lose its R, the abbreviation for right

parts.note: an augur was a Roman priest who foretold events from omens

indicators.note: the opening two letters of the word statements are taken

explanation.surface: An aged prophet makes a couple of pronouncements while missing something right.
explanation.definitionFit: August as an adjective means inspiring reverence and dignified, close kin to venerable.

clue.text: Renegade heads to another part of Alaska for one

indicators.note: the opening letters of another, part and of are taken

parts.note: Alaska is one of the American states

explanation.surface: A deserter heads off to a different region of Alaska.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name one who abandons a religion, party or cause, a traitor to a former faith.

clue.text: Drop off acquired work books

parts.note: got means obtained or acquired
op is short for opus, a work
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Someone nods off after picking up some reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop off' suggests falling asleep, but here it means to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: To decay or deteriorate is an idiomatic sense of drop off, as in standards dropping off.

clue.text: Forgetful, undergoing strain?

definitions.meaning: a memory full of holes lets things slip through
a strainer is a mesh utensil, so something being strained resembles one

explanation.surface: Absent-minded under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' reads as stress, but it is a pun on straining through a mesh.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a memory like a sieve means being forgetful, and a strainer is a sieve.

clue.text: Wordsworth's shivering started intermittently during wander

indicators.note: the picked letters go in the middle of the stroll word, happening during it

parts.note: to amble is to wander along at a leisurely pace

indicators.note: only every other letter of started is kept, as if it worked in fits

explanation.surface: A poet's shivering began in fits and starts while out rambling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intermittently' keeps the even letters of 'started'; 'during' puts them inside the stroll word. 'Wordsworth's' signals a poetic, archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: The poetic adjective meaning trembling or quivering is archaic, the sort of word a Romantic poet such as Wordsworth used.

clue.text: Actor Jeff grapples clearly after much beer — some here are disgusted?

indicators.note: the actor part follows the cask

parts.note: a tun is a large cask of beer

indicators.note: the actor's surname holds the adverb in its grip

parts.note: Jeff Bridges is an American film actor
well means clearly, as in seeing well

explanation.surface: After a lot of beer, the actor wrestles, and some onlookers are revolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgusted of Tunbridge Wells' is a stock British name for a pompous letter-writer to newspapers; the town is in Kent, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kent spa town is famous for its supposedly outraged residents who sign letters as Disgusted.

clue.text: Have fun with Jack cutting single over year

indicators.note: the card letter cuts into the reversed number
in a down entry, over turns the word for single upside down

parts.note: single means one
J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

explanation.surface: Having fun with Jack, cutting a single over a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' turns ONE into ENO; 'cutting' puts J inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enjoy something is to take pleasure in it, to have fun with it.

clue.text: Relatively rough pastry food in Birmingham, right at southern end

indicators.note: the pastry dish is put inside as food would be
the R for right is shifted to the bottom of the city word in this down entry

parts.note: Brum is an informal name for Birmingham, England's second city
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A rather coarse pie served in Birmingham, with something right at the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: Birmingham is England's second city. In a down entry the 'southern end' is the bottom, so 'right at southern end' shifts its R to the end before the pastry goes in.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of bumpy means more uneven, i.e. rougher than something else.

clue.text: Cry of disgust after man from Spain disrobed — no more!

indicators.note: the exclamation follows the stripped word
stripped of its outer layer, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: señor is Spanish for a man or gentleman
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A cry of revulsion after a Spaniard strips: stop it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disrobed' strips SENOR to ENO.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting this word demands that something stop, the same as crying no more.

clue.text: Cleaner look about kitchen essentially eliminated complaint

parts.note: a housemaid is a domestic cleaner

indicators.note: the look word goes about the leftover letters

parts.note: see means look

indicators.note: the essential middle of kitchen is removed, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A cleaner checks the kitchen and finds the problem gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially eliminated' strips kitchen to K and N, which 'about' puts inside SEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint here is a medical ailment: the bursitis caused by long kneeling while scrubbing floors.

clue.text: Enjoying nightlife perhaps, then to building with private

indicators.note: the words then to are being built into a fresh order

parts.note: something private is one's own, not shared

explanation.surface: Someone moves on to a building with a soldier, maybe for a night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier, but it means OWN, as in one's own. 'Building' rearranges THEN TO into ONTHET.
explanation.definitionFit: Being out for an evening's entertainment in bars and clubs is an idiom for enjoying nightlife.

clue.text: Very big okra presented with another starter

indicators.note: the dish name is given a different first letter in place of its own

parts.note: gumbo is another name for okra, the vegetable pods

explanation.surface: Okra served up alongside a different first course.
explanation.walkthrough: The new first letter is J, which the clue leaves the solver to find.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo is an adjective for something of huge size, as in a jumbo jet.

clue.text: Like certain models better/not as much?

parts.note: to top something is to better or beat it
less means a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A cryptic comparison of models that come out better or worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The slash splits two ideas: 'better' is the verb to top, and 'not as much' is less.
explanation.definitionFit: Some glamour models pose with no clothing above the waist, so they are described this way.

clue.text: Somewhere in E. Sussex, we hear pottery treated and heated, for example

indicators.note: the town's name is said aloud rather than spelt

parts.note: Rye is a small historic town in East Sussex, England
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain of the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A trip to a Sussex town where pottery is fired and treated.
explanation.walkthrough: RYE is a town in East Sussex, a county on England's south coast; MING is Chinese porcelain. The pair sounds like a word describing words that end in the same sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: The words treated and heated share their final sounds, so they are examples of words that chime with each other.

clue.text: African brothers facing current on banks of Tigris

parts.note: trade union members call one another brothers, so a TU stands for them

indicators.note: the outermost letters of Tigris, as banks lie at a river's edges

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current in physics

explanation.surface: Brothers walk beside the flowing Tigris.
explanation.walkthrough: TU, trade union, is fed by 'brothers', a union members' form of address; 'banks of' takes T and S from Tigris.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are a people of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa, so a member is an African.

clue.text: French wine keeps twelve months in Rome, on average

indicators.note: the wine holds the numeral within it

parts.note: Medoc is a red wine from the Bordeaux region of France
twelve months is one year, and one in Roman numerals is I
re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A French wine is laid down for a year in Rome, typically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On average' looks like one phrase, but 'on' is RE (about) and 'average' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mediocre is only ordinary and middling in quality, which is what average means.

clue.text: Rhonda, with gut being dodgy, discovers how booze is dispensed

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters go wrong and get rearranged

explanation.surface: Rhonda, with a dodgy stomach, finds out how beer is poured.
explanation.definitionFit: Draught beer is drawn from a cask or keg rather than served from a bottle.

clue.text: Left loaf after pea soup and fruit

indicators.note: the left and head parts come after the fog word

parts.note: a pea-souper is a thick fog, a kind of haze
loaf and nut are both slang for the head

explanation.surface: Left a loaf after pea soup and fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pea soup' is British slang for thick fog, and 'loaf' is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The cob or filbert is the edible nut of the hazel tree, classed as a fruit.

clue.text: Stupid middle-distance race perhaps around stream truncated

indicators.note: the race goes round the shortened stream word

parts.note: a one-mile race, written I MILE with the Roman numeral, is an example of a middle-distance event

indicators.note: the word for stream loses its last letter

parts.note: a beck is a small stream in northern England

explanation.surface: A foolish runner circles a short stream during a mile race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Truncated' cuts BECK to BEC. Imbecile is usually a noun, but it can also be used as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means foolish or idiotic, the same sense as stupid.

clue.text: Academic daughter wears clobber as Shakespeare character

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is an academic degree holder

indicators.note: the daughter letter is dressed in the hitting word

parts.note: to clobber is to hit, and to cuff is to hit

explanation.surface: A scholar's daughter puts on clothes to play a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like British slang for clothes, but here it is the verb to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Macduff is the Thane of Fife who kills Macbeth in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: More than one saying police rebuffed volunteers

indicators.note: turned back, so the police abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: the CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police
the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Many a remark when police turned back the volunteers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dicta is the plural of dictum, an authoritative pronouncement or maxim.

clue.text: Photographic gear welcome — it's needed for a fantastic creature

indicators.note: the greeting is required in place of the letter a

parts.note: a camera is photographic equipment
hi is a word of welcome

explanation.surface: A camera and a greeting are needed for a mythical beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's needed for a' puts HI in place of the first A of CAMERA.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera is a fire-breathing monster of Greek myth with a lion's head, goat's body and serpent's tail.

clue.text: Balance son, accompanied by cheers, on top of sibling

indicators.note: in a down entry the first parts sit above the sibling word

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, as cheers is
sis is short for sister, a sibling

explanation.surface: A son, with a toast, perches on his sister's shoulders.
explanation.walkthrough: TA and 'cheers' are both British for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Stasis is a state of equilibrium, a balance in which nothing changes.

clue.text: Historian Tom maybe returned suit when changed

indicators.note: the animal word is sent back, read from end to start

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, given as an example

indicators.note: the letters of suit are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Tom sent back the suit after it was altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' gives TAC; 'when changed' rearranges SUIT as ITUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitus was a Roman historian who wrote the Annals and Histories.

clue.text: Some Melba toast served up?

indicators.note: in a down entry, served up means the letters read upward
only part of the words Melba toast is used

explanation.surface: A little crisp toast is brought to the diners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' picks letters from Melba toast, and 'served up' reads them from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Toast is served on a dining surface, so the whole clue hints at where it ends up.

clue.text: Vet cut around site covering vein?

indicators.note: the word for cut is turned around

parts.note: to axe is to cut
a mine is a working dug over a vein of ore or coal

explanation.surface: A vet makes an incision near a spot covering a vein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vet' looks like the animal doctor, but it is the verb to check.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to check it carefully, the same as to inspect or scrutinise.

clue.text: Firework displays finally cease (time's gone) before 6th of November

indicators.note: only the last letter of displays is used
the T for time is taken out of the word for stop

parts.note: to quit is to cease

indicators.note: the sixth letter of November is taken

explanation.surface: Fireworks shows end before Bonfire Night, when time runs out.
explanation.walkthrough: Fireworks are let off in Britain on 5 November, Guy Fawkes Night, so the date fits the surface but only supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A squib is a small firework that hisses before it explodes.

clue.text: Checking van in lock-up, engineer altered tone

indicators.note: the front letter halts the shuffled word by sitting within it
the letters of engineer are put in another order
the van is the front, so the first letter of lock-up

explanation.surface: A van is held at a garage while an engineer retunes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' is the front, so 'van in lock-up' is L; 'Checking' puts it inside the rearranged ENGINEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Nile green is a pale bluish-green shade, so it is a tone of colour.

clue.text: What's possibly added to washing is frequently kept in reserve, after a spin

indicators.note: the word for frequently is held inside the spun short form
the short form is spun round to read backwards

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: Something added to the laundry is often held back after a spin cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' fits a washing machine, but here it turns RES into SER.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric conditioner is poured into a wash load to make clothes feel soft.

clue.text: Three successive characters painting house

parts.note: S, T and U are consecutive letters of the alphabet
painting is a form of art

explanation.surface: Three characters in a row paint a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Characters' are letters, and STU is one run of three in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: The royal house that ruled Scotland and later England bears this name.
